Brain fog isn’t just forgetfulness: What causes it? Is it linked to dementia? When should you worry?
Can’t focus, struggling to find the right word, or feeling like your brain is moving in slow motion? Experts explain what could be behind brain fog – including lack of sleep, stress, menopause and even dengue – whether it’s linked to dementia, and what you can do to think more clearly.
Some days are better than others, to reference a U2 song. Who hasn’t had a moment (or a few) when your brain simply says “no”? You lose your train of thought, can’t seem to focus, or have trouble finding the right word, phrase, term… you get the drift.
You chalk up the proverbial “brain fog” to a lack of sleep or the particularly stressful period you’re in. Perhaps it’s menopause beckoning from the hormonal pit that ageing has put you in. Or maybe, it’s a remnant from COVID-19. Wait, could it have been dengue?
“Defining brain fog is challenging due to the absence of a single universally accepted definition,” said Dr Jillian Teo, a senior psychologist from National Neuroscience Institute’s (NNI) Department of Psychology.
In general, she continued, brain fog refers to “a cluster of overlapping symptoms involving cognition, fatigue and mood”. So yes, it’s a mishmash of the abovementioned signs, plus difficulties in your processing speed.
“Some individuals may also report mental fatigue, confusion, or feeling overwhelmed by an overload of information,” said Dr Teo.
“Less obvious accompanying difficulties can include irritability, reduced tolerance for multitasking, making more everyday errors, and taking longer to complete familiar tasks,” said Dr Huang Wan Ping, the senior principal psychologist at Raffles HealthyLongevity.
“People may say, ‘my brain feels slow’, ‘I can’t think straight’, or ‘I have to read the same paragraph several times’.”
WHAT CAUSES BRAIN FOG?
Dr Huang highlighted that “sleep is an especially important and sometimes underestimated contributor”. “Sleep loss can affect attention, working memory, inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility, which depend substantially on networks involving the frontal regions of the brain.”
According to Dr Teo, “brain fog is frequently reported across a range of conditions and can arise from many different causes”, including the following:
- Infections and inflammation
- Nutritional deficiencies, such as being low on Vitamin B12 or iron
- Hormonal changes such as during peri- and menopause, thyroid problems
- Changes in brain chemicals, such as acetylcholine, dopamine and noradrenaline, that affect attention and alertness
- Poor and disrupted sleep, including jetlag
- Stress
- High and low blood sugar levels
- Physical exhaustion and fatigue
- Alcohol consumption
- Traumatic brain injury
- Substance abuse
WHAT’S HAPPENING IN THE BRAIN?
“The prefrontal cortex (front part of the brain) and frontoparietal network (the brain’s cognitive control centre) are particularly important because they help us maintain attention, manipulate information, prioritise relevant information, and suppress distractions,” explained Dr Huang.
“When the brain is sleep deprived, fatigued, physiologically stressed or unwell, the efficiency of these systems can decrease. The person may still possess the knowledge or memory but accessing it can become slower and more effortful,” said Dr Huang.
However, he hesitated to pin brain fog on any singular neuron or neurotransmitter. “There is currently no single neurotransmitter, brain region or biological mechanism that explains all experiences of brain fog. Thinking clearly requires several brain systems to work together efficiently,” said Dr Huang. “I would describe brain fog less as ‘neurons malfunctioning’ and more as the brain temporarily becoming less efficient at allocating cognitive resources.”
HOW LONG DOES BRAIN FOG USUALLY LAST?
The experts don’t have a specific answer. “The severity, frequency and duration of brain fog vary considerably across individuals, depending on the cause,” said Dr Teo.
For instance, “sleep-related brain fog may improve after restorative sleep, while stress-related symptoms may fluctuate over days or weeks”, explained Dr Huang. “Cognitive symptoms associated with conditions such as long COVID-19 can persist for months or longer. Brain fog can also fluctuate according to sleep, fatigue, illness, stress, and cognitive demand.”
BESIDES COVID-19, CAN OTHER VIRAL INFECTIONS ALSO CAUSE BRAIN FOG?
Much has been said about long COVID-19 symptoms – one of which is the infamous brain fog. But before the pandemic hit, experts have already suspected that brain fog might also be seen in other viral infections such as dengue.
In fact, a 2024 study by Nanyang Technological University (NTU) researchers found that those who contracted dengue faced a 213-per-cent increased risk of cognition or memory disorders. The study had looked at tests and the medical claim records of 11,707 Singapore residents with dengue between July 2021 and October 2022.
To also examine the dengue-and-brain connection, Singapore General Hospital’s Dr Shirin Kalimuddin, a senior consultant from Department of Infectious Diseases, recruited 209 patients with acute viral infections such as dengue and followed them for up to a year – right before the pandemic struck in 2019. Of the lot, 48 patients had dengue.
ARE THERE FOODS THAT ELIMINATE BRAIN FOG?
There are no specific foods that have been proven to prevent or eliminate brain fog, said Dr Jillian Teo, a senior psychologist from National Neuroscience Institute’s Department of Psychology.
What good nutrition does is reduce neuroinflammation and support the gut-brain axis, which is a two-way communication network that links your central nervous system with your digestive tract, she said. To do that, it helps to keep a balanced and nutrient-dense diet rich in fibre, omega-3 fatty acids, antioxidants, and minimally processed foods.
The results confirmed the link as well. In a paper published in 2022, Dr Shirin noted that almost all of the patients (95.8 per cent of dengue patients; 94 per cent of patients with other acute viral respiratory infections) “experienced at least one symptom of fatigue, somnolence (a state of extreme drowsiness), headache, concentration impairment or memory impairment within the first week of enrolment”.
The SGH study showed that those “neurological symptoms that persist can also be an issue after other infections, such as dengue”, said Dr Nicole Keong, a senior consultant and neurosurgeon at Department of Neurosurgery, NNI.
“Symptoms may include memory difficulties, concentration, thinking speed, fatigue, balance, or changes in or loss of the sense of smell – and they can have a long-term impact on daily activities and quality of life.”
But as to how dengue causes brain fog, “the mechanism for this is still unknown”, said Dr Keong. “It is also unclear how long brain fog and related symptoms last for.”
To study the effects dengue has on the brain, Dr Keong and her team are currently recruiting dengue patients for the NEurodegeneration & Understanding of Risk Overlay in Neuroimaging (NEURON3) study. To date, they have found “altered brain signatures” in dengue patients in the chronic stage. “However, it is too early in our study to be able to interpret what those changes mean,” said Dr Keong.
“By studying the impact of these common infections on our brain health, we aim to contribute to a deeper understanding of how the brain responds to and recovers from threats to its functioning, following infection and injury,” said Dr Keong.
WHAT ABOUT MENOPAUSE?
“In women experiencing perimenopause, declining oestrogen levels can contribute significantly to experiences of brain fog,” said Dr Teo.
Oestrogen helps support glucose metabolism, synaptic function and the balance of neurotransmitters, she explained. “As oestrogen levels decrease, the brain becomes less efficient at glucose metabolism, particularly in regions such as the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex that are critical for memory, attention, and executive functioning.”
The good news is, the cognitive complaints that many women have during the menopausal transition often stabilise following menopause, said Dr Teo. “However, some women continue to report difficulties with memory, attention and processing speed, with such complaints being more frequently reported among postmenopausal than premenopausal women.”
DOES HAVING HAD BRAIN FOG MEAN YOU ARE MORE PRONE TO DEMENTIA?
“Brain fog itself has not been established as a cause of dementia,” said Dr Huang. “Someone experiencing transient brain fog because of sleep deprivation, stress or illness should not conclude that they are developing dementia.”
Rather, “dementia risk is influenced by a range of established factors, including age, cardiovascular and metabolic health, genetics, lifestyle factors, and underlying brain pathology”, said Dr Teo.
While brain fog and dementia can share some symptoms, particularly forgetfulness and difficulty concentrating, the clinical patterns can be very different, according to Dr Huang. “Brain fog often fluctuates. People commonly remain aware of their cognitive difficulties, and performance may vary according to fatigue, stress or sleep.”
Nevertheless, said Dr Teo, persistent and progressive cognitive changes should not be dismissed as "just brain fog". Dementia that occurs in the 40s and 50s may present atypically, with symptoms progressively worsening over months to years despite management, she said.
Look out for significant language or word-finding difficulties; personality or behavioural changes; declining ability to manage activities in daily living; and a family history of young-onset dementia, advised Dr Teo.
CAN EXERCISE HELP WITH BRAIN FOG?
“Exercise may not ‘clear’ brain fog immediately but regular physical activity can support brain and body function, helping with focus, energy and coordination,” said senior physiotherapist Choo Kai Bing from 365 Cancer Prevention Society.
Try activities that challenge both mind and movement. Dancing is a good option as you have to remember sequences and coordinate your steps. Or try pickleball, where you have to track the ball and react quickly. “These activities help strengthen the connection between what your brain sees and processes, and how your body responds,” said Choo.
The same goes for women with menopause-related brain fog. Cognitive complaints, such as difficulties with attention, memory and concentration, can impact performance at work, social relationships, confidence and overall wellbeing, said Dr Teo.
To sum it up, “the sensible response to persistent brain fog is not to assume dementia”, said Dr Huang. “But neither should we simply ignore it; a medical assessment can help identify and address the underlying cause.”
WHAT CAN YOU DO TO MANAGE BRAIN FOG?
Here’s what the experts suggest you can do to tackle the various cognitive issues that come with brain fog:
- Trouble focusing and organising your thoughts
Avoid multitasking. Instead, do one task at a time, suggested Sarah Zheng, a counsellor from 365 Cancer Prevention Society. If it’s a big task, break it into smaller steps – and give yourself time to complete each step, she said.
To help you further, Dr Huang recommended reducing your environmental distractions, such as closing unnecessary tabs on your browser and silencing your notifications.
- Poor memory
“Attention is the gateway to memory,” said Dr Huang. “If you are replying to messages while in a meeting, and thinking about your next appointment, information may never be properly encoded. This can create a cycle where we become convinced that ‘my memory is terrible’ when the underlying issue may be that we were not able to give the information our full attention in the first place.”
Sometimes, improving attention at the point of learning is a better strategy, said Dr Huang. “When we want to achieve more, it can help to start with doing less. Be present and focus on one thing at a time.”
- Slow at processing new information
Tell yourself that it is okay to take more time to process the information and respond, said Zheng. “Avoid rushing important decisions. Note down important information if needed.”
Dr Teo suggested using external memory aids such as calendars, reminder apps, and checklists to minimise your cognitive load of holding large volumes of information. Mnemonic techniques (such as using acronyms, stories, or rhymes), visualisation, or chunking information into smaller, more manageable pieces may also support learning and recall, she added.
And no, you’re not copping out or “giving in” to brain fog when you use these aids, said Dr Huang. “In neuropsychological rehabilitation, we call these compensatory strategies, which means using the environment to reduce cognitive load.”
- Difficulty finding a word
Allow yourself extra time to retrieve the word without panicking, advised Dr Teo. This can be helpful as stress can further interfere with word retrieval. “Strategies such as describing the concept, paraphrasing, or returning to the word later can often be helpful.”
- Mental exhaustion
If you find yourself mentally powering down during office hours, especially in the afternoon, naturopath Sebastian Liew of Leaf To Life, suggested running cool water from your elbows down your forearms as well as applying cool water to your nape to recharge. “Do not towel dry; just wipe the excess,” he said. It also helps to walk away from your desk for a while to break the stagnant energy, he said.
For an afternoon snack, opt for an apple for better blood sugar control, rather than sugar-loaded biscuits and sweets that spike and crash your blood sugar levels, Liew said.
- Struggling to wind down after work
“If it is not possible to screen-fast because of a late assignment, take a cool lower body shower after work,” suggested Liew. Again, do not towel dry but wipe excess water only.
To help you calm your mind and get ready for bed, Liew suggested diaphragmatic breathing:
- Sit comfortably in your bed with your back straight.
- Close your eyes and inhale for four counts (your belly should rise). Slowly exhale for eight counts (your belly should fall).
- If any stressful moment or image comes to your mind, admit the resulting emotion to yourself by thinking “I am angry/worried/frustrated" etc. Don’t suppress or deny your feelings.
- As you breathe, recall and visualise someone, something or somewhere that regenerates positive feelings of gratitude or love. The main thing is to recreate the feeling, not intellectual thinking. Or you can recall moments of your creativity, laughter and joy. Stay with the feeling for at least two minutes.

- To complete the Frigate puzzle in Arc Raiders, players have to first board it using the Arc Reclaimer.
- Next, they have to look for Power Cores and break them.
- Finally, players have to lower the Cargo and leave with it to complete the challenge.
Arc Raiders Frozen Trail update has completely changed the game. It has added so much new content, but the highlight of the update is the Frigate map condition. Completing the Frigate map condition is extremely challenging. But if you are determined to complete it, here is a full Arc Raiders Frigate guide for you.
Arc Raiders Frigate Map Condition Explained
Frigate is the new Arc Raiders map condition released with the Frozen Trail update. You don’t need to play the Pendola Pass map to get this map condition, as it happens on all Arc Raiders maps. This map condition adds a massive flying arc to the game that shoots down anything below. Players must board this Frigate and sabotage it to get all the loot. During this map condition, here are the conditions applied to the map:
- No active locked doors
- Decreased amount of overall loot value
- No active Raider Hatches
- No Free Loadout
One thing unique about the Arc Raiders Frigate map condition is that players cannot take a free loadout to play it. This is likely to prevent players from camping other raiders, as the Arc Frigate event requires a ton of resources to complete.
How to Prepare for Frigate in Arc Raiders
Arc Raiders Frigate map condition is extremely hard, and players will need to be properly equipped to even get close to completing it. Here is how you need to prepare for the Arc Raiders Frigate challenge:
First, players will need one Heavy Ammo weapon, along with one Energy Ammo or Launcher Ammo weapon. This is because players will need to fight a ton of Arcs and break the Power Cores inside the Frigate, which requires a ton of Arc penetration damage. Ideally, I prefer Bettina for the heavy weapon as it is both good for PvP and PvE. Check our Arc Raiders weapon tier list to know about the best weapons in the game.
This is the ideal setup you can prepare to take on the Frigate in Arc Raiders:
- 1x Bettina (or any other heavy weapon)
- 1x Hullcracker or 1x Jupiter
- 1x Looting MK3 Survivor (for the additional slots)
- 1x Medium Shield
- 2 Stacks of Herbal Bandages
- 1 Stack of Vita Shot or 1 Stack of Sterilized Bandage
- 3 Stacks of Shield Recharger (two small and one medium)
- 2x Wolf Packs or 2 stacks of Trigger Nade
- 3x Barriers
- 2x Defibrillator
- 1x Snaphook
- Heavy and Launcher/Energy Ammo (fill all the remaining slots)
Now, you can obviously change your setup based on your lobby type. If you get highly PvP lobbies, getting a better PvP weapon might be better, along with some mines. However, this setup should be enough to take down the Frigate without anyone spoiling your plans. Also, make sure to use the best Arc Raiders skill tree build for further advantage.
Arc Raiders Frigate Puzzle Guide
The Frigate puzzle is quite simple, but the threat of PvP players and the massive number of flying arcs, along with Hydras, makes it an incredibly hard challenge. But if you have prepared as mentioned above, you should be able to complete the puzzle by following the steps below.
How to Board the Frigate in Arc Raiders
To complete the Arc Raiders Frigate guide, you will first need to board it. To board the Frigate, you will need to board the Arc Reclaimers. These are small arcs that keep coming down from the Frigate and going back up. Track them when they reach the ground and climb them.
You will see the option to disrupt them now. Do it, and it will take you straight up to the Frigate. Now comes the hard part: sabotaging the Frigate by breaking the Power Cores.
All Frigate Power Cores Locations
Once you have boarded the Frigate, you will have to break all the Power Cores on it. This can be done by you or your team alone, or others can also help you out. Here are all the Power Core locations on the Frigate that you need to break:
Power Core Location 1:
- After boarding, go inside until you reach a place with a button showing ‘Move Up’. Skip this for now and continue on your way to the other end and circle to the other side.
- Here you will find the first Power Core. Shoot it down.
Power Core Location 2:
- Now, head back to the button area. Here you can either use Snap Hook to get up directly, or two players have to push the buttons on either side to lift one player.
- Once that player is up, they can interact with the button there to move the other players up.
- Players have to then go in and interact with the three buttons there to lift up the main coil.
Power Core Location 3:
- Before opening up the main coil, players can find two power coils above.
- Simply look up to find them on either side.
Power Core Location 4:
- Once you have broken the main power core and the ones above, along with defeating all the arcs, you will need to get to the top of the Frigate.
- You can either snap-hook from the side of the main coil to the ledge above, or break the yellow buttons on the wall to bring down walls for climbing.
- Above, you will have to breach the wall containers to expose the Power Core inside.
Power Core Location 5:
- Continue up to the very top of the Frigate and break the Power Cores there.
- Make sure to set up barriers here to hide from arcs.
Power Core Location 6:
- Finally, you will be able to enter the Frigate. Inside, keep breaking yellow buttons to open doors and look for all the Power Cores.
- They will always be inside locked rooms, so they will be easy to find.
- Break all the Power Cores inside to reach the Cargo at the very bottom.
Drop Cargo and Leave Frigate in Arc Raiders
Finally, you will reach the Cargo. There, you will have to interact with the four sides, where you will have to breach the containers first. Next, there will be two interactable buttons on both sides of the cargo. Press it together repeatedly to keep dropping the cargo. When the cargo completely drops, jump on it and leave the Frigate with it.
Once you reach the ground, you can loot the Cargo easily, and it will have some of the best loot you can find during the map condition.
All Arc Raiders Frigate Rewards
There are many lootable things in the Frigate, especially if you keep opening the containers along the way without waiting for the final cargo. All of these have generic industrial and mechanical materials, but the main items you can get from them are:
- Amplification Modules
- Research items
Amplification Modules are needed to modify your weapons, and Research items can be used to obtain research points in the Arc Raiders Outpost. Other than these, the Frigate holds many epic and legendary rewards, but we haven’t seen many blueprints or guns drop yet.
So, that’s the full Arc Raiders Frigate guide. Have any questions? Ask us in the comments section below.

Evangelizing to his 512,000 TikTok followers occasionally requires that dating coach Chad Franklin post the private communications of his clients, who pay upwards of $5,000 for his services.
In September, Franklin shared a DM conversation in which a woman implied she couldn’t afford an Uber with the text overlay “Don’t date POOR women!!!” That same month, he uploaded a video of a client’s successful text exchange on Hinge where they talked about the need to “flirt over some margaritas.” In the clip, Franklin can barely contain himself, noting that it was the type of tête-à-tête that gets his “dick hard”: “This is what men are looking for. We lead, you follow.”
Franklin posts under the alias @DefundSimping, and has made it his mission to help straight, career-driven guys in their “post-breakup, post-divorce” era undo their “simp” behavior, which he defines as putting women on a pedestal or giving them too much attention.
I reached out to the 30-year-old content creator because I wanted to talk about Hinge’s decision to start testing screenshot protection in India. The announcement set off a firestorm of reaction across social media last week, rekindling a debate around digital etiquette, privacy, and shame.
“Everyone who’s downloaded the app has seen the debauchery and the drama,” Franklin says, explaining that being online in 2026 simply means there is a chance you will become the day’s main character whether you intended to or not. “People are aware that they could be the next haha moment, but that doesn't mean they deserve it.”
TikTokers, X accounts like @hingestrange, and other online creators have built entire brands out of screenshotting and sharing bizarre dating profile prompts, cringe pickup lines, or red flags found while swiping. But critics of the trend argue it’s a form of public humiliation that should end.
In response to news of Hinge revoking profile screenshotting ability in India, some responded with relief.
“People on here kinda turned being on a dating app into both an extension of the panopticon and a window into their own personal penchant for cruelty,” writer Tres Dean noted on X. “I actually think this might be the first ethical development in online dating in years if not ever.”
X user @randy_mossad added, “Better for a million cheaters to go unpunished than for one regular person looking for love to get humiliated by leaked chats.”
In a TikTok video, Florida-based creator Kiara said she understands the change despite having posted screenshots to shame men who were hypersexual or “super disrespectful” in their profiles. “But I’ve noticed now that we’re in an ‘I hate men’ apocalypse ... women are posting men’s profiles simply because they’re not just not attracted to them,” she continued, describing the latter as being “wrong” and “mean.”
At a moment when the apps feel broken for so many people, there seems to be a desire for more private, less performative forms of dating and communication.
While apps like Raya and Grindr already include screenshot protection, the India pilot is the first iteration of it for Hinge, which will block screenshots on surfaces containing personally identifiable profile information, including Discover, Likes You, and Standouts.
The company confirms to WIRED that testing in India is part of an initiative to help singles build trust among other users and with the platform. The insights will determine whether and how Hinge introduces the feature in additional markets, but there are no current plans to greenlight screenshot protection in US or other regions.
A 2025 study in the Journal of Computer-Mediated Communication suggested that screenshots create “privacy turbulence” by allowing a recipient to permanently store and redistribute private conversations without the original sender's knowledge or consent, noting that the screenshot feature eliminates a shared boundary of control and strips away context.
But for some women in particular, screenshotting profiles has become a necessary precaution when vetting potential suitors. “Privacy’s in tension with safety. Screenshots can document inappropriate behavior or allow someone to check in with a friend before meeting a stranger,” says Lizzie Li, a communications researcher, who adds that communities like Are We Dating the Same Guy? grew partly out of women sharing screenshots to address safety concerns.
Asked whether the company has an obligation to prevent users from having their profiles turned into public content—30 million people currently use the app—a Hinge spokesperson tells WIRED that screenshot protection, along with Comment Filter and Did This Bother You?, is “another way we’re exploring how to help daters control how and where personal details are shared.” Singles will still be able to screenshot their messages with other matches if they want to report an account for potential safety concerns, affording women an extra layer of defense on dating apps where they disproportionately experience harassment and privacy violations. According to Hinge’s community guidelines, harassment, bullying, and intimidation are prohibited.
“When you are a bystander, it is fairly obvious that a privacy violation is occurring and most people would not want it to happen to them. At the same time, discomfort has not stopped the behavior,” says Alexis Ingber, an assistant professor at Syracuse University whose research focuses on privacy and emerging tech. “Dating-profile dunking reflects a broader sense of entitlement to others’ data.”
But Franklin, who has a knack for speaking in clip-ready one-liners, doesn’t believe dating apps have a duty to protect users from becoming a punch line on social media. “If you enter the dragon’s den, you may get bit by the dragon,” he tells me.
Still, with 20 clients on his roster, he says he does his best to block “every name, lip, face, and eye, trying to keep people private” when posting screenshots, because he understands that people are “scared of getting hit-pieced.” Before ending our Zoom call to meet with another client, he tells me there is actually one way to completely sidestep the problem. “If you don’t want to be potentially doxed, just don’t get on a dating app. Go talk to a girl at a dog park. Go to a farmer's market. Do it the old-fashioned way.”

The Kerala High Court order asking the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau to register an FIR against former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T. Veena, and his son-in-law and MLA P.A. Mohamed Riyas, has raised larger questions of natural justice and court orders overlooking the statutory provisions of law, according to legal experts.
Though the single judge elaborately heard the petitioner K.M. Shajahan and the Enforcement Directorate, which forwarded a letter to the State government seeking to register an FIR against the trio, the three were not offered an opportunity to be heard. The denial of the opportunity to be heard could be construed as the denial of natural justice. It will legally enable Mr. Vijayan and the two others to challenge the single judge’s order before the High Court or Supreme Court, judicial sources pointed out.
The order of the single judge, according to some legal experts, bypassed Section 17 (A) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, which mandated prior approval from the competent authority for police officers to conduct inquiry into offences committed by public servants in the discharge of their official functions.
As a safeguard
The Section was introduced through an amendment in 2018 as a safeguard for government servants against unnecessary litigation, which could deter them from discharging their duties in an honest and fair manner. The question whether a court can overlook the statutory provisions of law that mandate prior approval for booking the case is pending before the Supreme Court. The matter was left for the consideration of a larger Bench of the court as the judges who heard the challenge came out with opposing judgments. Hence, the legality of the single judge’s action in ordering the registration of the FIR too could be challenged before the appropriate forum, sources indicated.
The State government, represented by Advocate General K. Jaju Babu, had contended that the competent authority should have an option to register an FIR or conduct a preliminary inquiry on receiving information from the ED. The State, which is left with limited legal options following the order, is unlikely to go on appeal.
The State could have played a crucial role in deciding the fate of the case had its prior sanction been sought under Section 17 (A) of the Act to prosecute the three. The legal responsibility of challenging the decision is left with Mr. Vijayan and the two others, legal sources indicated.
Does not apply to Veena
Meanwhile, the Vigilance will have to book an FIR against Mr. Vijayan and Mr. Riyas under the provisions of the Act. The ED would make use of the FIR and the allegations of corruption as a predicate offence to book Mr. Vijayan and Ms. Riyas for money laundering under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The Act will not apply to Ms. Veena who is not a public servant. However, the ED had proceeded against her based on the criminal complaint filed by the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) in relation to the alleged corporate fraud committed in Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) and Exalogic Solutions Pvt. Ltd., the firm owned by her.
Incidentally, the fate of the case against Ms. Veena would depend upon the outcome of the petition filed by CMRL before the Delhi High Court challenging the SFIO investigation.

Leaves are a problem of addition by subtraction: Just a couple of mature trees can drop enough debris that you need to remove, and in the process, consume hours of your weekends. Mowing leaves into mulch is a compelling option, but you’ll still need to wrangle them off driveways, walkways, flower beds, and patios. Gas blowers have long been the standard, but rising noise bans, finicky engines that are hard to start, and battery advances are cutting into their appeal.
If you’re on the fence about a leaf blower, know that owning one of any kind will reduce the amount of raking you do, but rarely eliminate it. For small yards, or if you (or your neighbor) have just one medium-sized deciduous tree, a rake and a tarp may be all you need. On the other hand, if you live in an arboretum, the long runtime of a gas backpack blower may be worth the maintenance headaches—unless you’re willing to invest heavily in multiple batteries.
I’ve tested the newest crop of battery-powered blowers on everything from heavy fabric leaves to gravel, mulch, and even knocking over a concrete paver. Today’s models deliver serious clearing power without the gas-can hassle, though runtime is always the primary trade-off. Here’s everything you need to know about battery-powered blowers.
Featured
Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.
Best Overall
When factoring in overall performance along with the quality and diversity of Ego’s outdoor tool ecosystem, this blower is the best option for most users. In testing, it delivered gaslike power, easily knocking over a 5-pound brick paver on high speed where lesser machines required turbo mode, and it cleared the test patch of leaves without issue, without relying on turbo. Even with all that power, it was the second-quietest machine on turbo, registering about 89.7 decibels at an arm’s-length distance of 30 inches—though Ego still suggests hearing protection.

It had the shortest runtime of the tested models, a direct trade-off for its high performance. FAQs
What to Look for (and What to Skip) in a Leaf Blower
Here’s what I’d focus on when buying a blower for leaf cleanup:
Volts: In the cordless power-tool arms race, leaf blower batteries range from 18 to 80 volts. Some of that difference is marketing trickery: an advertised 20-volt max battery or tool delivers essentially the same power as an 18-volt model, and the same goes for 36- and 40-volt options. But, unless you’re a minimalist who wants one battery to power everything from a drill/driver to lawn and garden gear, you’ll probably be happier with a leaf blower that uses at least a 36-volt battery. A few capable 18-volt blowers use two batteries—either simultaneously to mimic the power of a 36-volt tool or in succession to increase the runtime—but they tend to cost more and only make sense if you already own the batteries. For smaller jobs, though, a standard, single-battery 18- or 20-volt blower may be all you need to clear a patio, clean out the garage or shed, or dry a car.
Amps: Volts get most of the marketing attention on the box, but a battery’s amp-hour rating tells you more about how long a blower runs. Think of voltage as the car’s engine and amp-hours as the size of the gas tank—you want to know both. Batteries with higher amp-hour ratings cost more than otherwise-similar battery voltages, and they tend to be heavier. For leaf blowers, manufacturers typically pair kits with batteries rated from 4 to 8 amp-hours. You can buy higher-capacity batteries separately, and it pays to know the range of options a manufacturer has. A battery with a higher amp-hour typically takes longer to charge.
Systems: Underestimating the range of tools a battery can power in pursuit of “the best” is, in my opinion, a mistake. Often, the difference between two top-performing tools is negligible, and with cordless power tools, that difference often comes down to runtime, which you can address with a higher-capacity battery. If your garage is already stocked with one brand’s outdoor power equipment (OPE), it makes sense to stay within that platform and buy the blower as a bare tool, leveraging the batteries you already have. Switching brands just to buy “the best” probably isn’t worth it to introduce a whole new battery and charger.
If you’re new to OPE—and a leaf blower is a common first purchase—the breadth of tools that share the battery matters. Some manufacturers stick to the lawn and garden basics, so one battery can power a blower, mower, string trimmer, and hedge trimmer, while others offer a much wider range of tools, from log splitters to snow blowers, and even some handy lifestyle products like portable power stations. Before buying, consider what else you can power with the battery that comes with your leaf blower because, chances are, lording over leaves won’t be your only lawn and garden chore.
Traditional 18-volt power tool manufacturers—the ones who make drill/drivers and circular saws—all offer leaf blowers and the simplicity of a one-battery platform, but they’re not powerful enough to replace a gas unit. Ryobi, for example, uses 18-volt batteries across its traditional power tools, and some outdoor equipment, but its most capable gas alternative options run on 40-volt batteries.
Detent clasp: Blowers have two or more connection points: where the tube meets the housing and where the nozzle attaches to the tube. Look for models with a detent at those junctions—a small, often brightly colored spring-loaded clip that snaps into place with a satisfying click when the parts connect. I find these connections hold more securely and last longer than simple friction-fit attachments.
Stubby nozzle: Recently, blowers aimed at car detailers, with short tubes and sometimes a pistol grip, have become popular. Manufacturers responded by adding a stubby, 3- to 6-inch tube that the main blower attachment slides over. When you remove the longer tube, this short one works to direct the volume of air with an overall shorter tool length that’s easier to use around cars or in tight spots (the blower’s nozzle doesn’t fit on this stubby tube, though, so you lose some velocity).
What I’d Worry Less About:
Weight: Across the board, regardless of voltage, a good battery-powered blower will weigh about 10.5 pounds with the battery attached. If you need a lighter option, look for an 18-volt powered blower. Some have better balance than others, meaning that when you hold them without squeezing the trigger, as you would while walking around, the tool stays mostly level or the nozzle end tips down a bit. These models will cause less fatigue than one that forces you to rotate the nozzle upward. With the former, you only need to make a slight horizontal twisting motion to spread the stream of air. Most modern leaf blowers also draw air in a straight line through the rear of the tool, unlike gas-powered models with intakes mounted to the left or right of the engine. Those offset intakes can create a twisting motion that increases hand fatigue and may even suck in your pant leg.
CFM, MPH, and Newton: This sounds counterintuitive, considering how much marketing goes into boasting about a leaf blower’s cubic feet per minute (CFM) and MPH, but these figures are a guide, not necessarily the only reason to buy a specific model. A blower needs both to be useful: CFM tells you how much air it moves, while MPH tells you how fast that air is moving. But there’s no universally adopted testing method for these specifications when it comes to battery-powered blowers (ANSI/OPEI B175.2, the standard test on the books, applies only to internal combustion engines). That means brands can test their units differently — for example, measuring MPH where the motor meets the tube rather than at the end of the blower tube, which gives you a better sense of the airspeed you’ll actually get in use. Some CFM numbers are also measured with the unit running in its max, boost, or turbo setting, rather than on high speed.
Newtons, a unit of force, is a rating that’s appearing more frequently on the spec sheets of higher-voltage, battery-powered leaf blowers and is the best apples-to-apples comparison of blowing power. However, because there’s no testing code for battery-powered leaf blowers, reporting newtons is optional and, like CFM and MPH, consumers have no way of knowing whether the test is standardized. Generally speaking, a good midrange blower will produce around 20 newtons, while models that produce more are typically higher-performing units. Treat newtons as a guide rather than a definitive specification while buying.
Wide nozzles: Some blowers come with a wide-tip nozzle, which can be useful for clearing paved surfaces like patios and driveways or blowing water off flat surfaces. But in practice, it’s not enough of a game changer to be a deciding factor. The narrower nozzle is typically what you’ll use, and you can twist your hand back and forth to create a wider pattern when needed.
How Noisy Are Battery-Powered Leaf Blowers?
When tested from 30 inches away to approximate the noise you’d hear at arm’s length, the blowers ranged from 78.6 decibels on high to 95.2 decibels on turbo. Most user manuals recommend wearing hearing protection when using these tools, particularly for extended periods. By comparison, a handheld gas blower might produce 100 to 110 decibels. That might not sound like a lot more noise, but generally, a 10-decibel increase is perceived by the ear as roughly twice as loud.
Much of the noise reduction comes from eliminating the idling gas engine. Your neighbors will thank you for going battery-powered, too: In open air, sound typically drops by about 6 decibels each time you double your distance from the source. That means your neighbor across the street might hear your battery-powered blower at roughly the same volume as standing next to a washing machine.
What Else Are Battery-Powered Leaf Blowers Good For?
Besides clearing leaves and grass clippings, these fume-free tools are handy for all sorts of jobs. Use one to dry wet surfaces after rain or washing, including your car, patio furniture, or deck. In winter, a blower can remove a light dusting of snow from your car, making it easier to clear areas like the roof. With a cautious trigger finger, you can also clear dry leaves from gutters—just avoid wet, matted debris, which will only turn into a mess below. When grilling or firing up a pizza oven or outdoor fire pit, a gentle stream of air from a safe distance can help get the flames going. Indoors, a blower can clear dust from baseboard heating assemblies or remove lint from your dryer vent.
How I Tested Battery-Powered Leaf Blowers
I put each blower through a series of tests to gauge power, runtime, noise, and ease of use. I spread about 8,800 3x3-inch polyester crafting leaves—nearly 4 pounds’ worth—over a measured 6-by-6-foot area and used each blower to clear the section, noting which models could do the job on high and which required a boost or turbo mode. To test blowing power, I placed a 5-pound concrete paver a fixed distance from the nozzle and recorded which machines could knock it over on high and which needed turbo.
For runtime, I fully charged each battery, ran the blower at its highest standard speed, excluding any turbo or max settings, and timed how long it lasted. I measured noise with a smartphone decibel-meter app held 30 inches from the air intake while each blower ran on high and at any available turbo or max setting. I also performed practical tests to see how well each model moved gravel and wood chips and cleared water from surfaces such as a grill and patio furniture.

Rathi Med Speciality Hospital, Chennai, launched a fresh meniscus allograft transplantation (MAT) programme as part of the Chennai Knee Course 2026 on Sunday (October 4).
The programme was inaugurated by IIT-Madras Director V. Kamakoti and Tamil Nadu Health Secretary Darez Ahamed, IAS.
The programme involves using a healthy meniscus from selected patients undergoing total knee replacement as a fresh graft for patients whose damaged meniscus cannot be repaired or reconstructed.
The hospital said it had received a licence from the Tamil Nadu government to perform fresh meniscus transplantation of the knee ), valid until December 2030.
The programme is led by N. Ragunanthan, Director, Head of Orthopaedics, and Consultant Surgeon of the hospital.
The conference, titled ‘The Meniscus 360° – From Repair to Transplant’, discussed meniscus transplantation and knee preservation.
The hospital also presented its Kinematic Knee Treatment and KPA Knee Preservation 360° approach for knee preservation in suitable patients below 60 years of age.

Medicine and surgery are not the answer for overweight children, the World Health Organization said Wednesday.
Releasing its first guidelines addressing the sharp rise in obesity among children and adolescents, the WHO instead strongly recommended structured diets, physical activity and behaviour changes.
"WHO does not recommend pharmacological treatment, bariatric surgery (surgery that changes the stomach or digestive tract) or weight-loss devices for children aged 0-9 years," it said.
"For adolescents aged 10-19 years, treatment with approved medicines may be considered only when a supervised multimodal lifestyle programme has not achieved the desired results.
"Bariatric surgery may be considered under strict conditions for adolescents with severe obesity."
The recommendations for those aged 19 and under contrast with the UN health agency's guidelines for adult obesity issued in December 2025, following the surge in popularity of a new generation of appetite-suppressing drugs called GLP-1 agonists -- which includes blockbuster brands Ozempic and Mounjaro.
The WHO said the range of weight-loss and diabetes drugs could be used for tackling obesity -- in adults.
170 million affected
In 2024, some 70 million children aged five to nine were obese, as were 100 million adolescents aged 10 to 19 worldwide, according to the WHO.
Among 5- to 19-year-olds, the prevalence of obesity has surged globally, rising from two percent in 1990 to eight percent in 2024.
"The rise of obesity is observed everywhere in all regions," said Luz Maria De Regil, director of the WHO's nutrition and food safety department.
"It's growing in low- and middle-income countries," while some high-income countries are starting to stop the rise of obesity, without yet making reductions.
"The foundation of obesity care for children and adolescents is not medicine or surgery, but access to comprehensive support that enables healthy eating, physical activity and sustainable behaviour change," she said.
The recommendations also stressed the importance of addressing mental health alongside obesity.
Anxiety, depression and low self-esteem can contribute to unhealthy eating, physical inactivity and social withdrawal, the WHO said.
Children and adolescents living with obesity may experience stigma and bullying, the UN health agency added.
Maria Nieves Garcia Casal, a scientist in the WHO's nutrition and food safety department, told reporters that bariatric surgery may be considered during adolescence for cases of severe obesity accompanied by complications such as type 2 diabetes or hypertension -- if diet and lifestyle changes have failed.

The Riyadh International Humanitarian Forum on 24-25 February 2025 brought together global partners from the humanitarian sector to discuss urgent health and humanitarian issues. It focused on advocacy for the survival, health diplomacy, well-being, and dignity of people affected by crises, as well as the security of aid workers. The forum, marking the 10th anniversary of the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSRelief), witnessed key agreements and pledges aimed at addressing ongoing humanitarian challenges in the Middle East and beyond.
KSRelief Supervisor-General, Abdullah Al Rabeeah, and Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General signing funding agreements in response to humanitarian crises. Photo by: WHO/Karim Yassmineh
WHO and KSrelief signed new agreements aimed at malaria prevention and cholera control in Yemen. This includes a US$ 12 million for malaria control and US$ 2.1 million to expand cholera treatment. Another agreement, worth US$ 3.6 million, was made between KSrelief and WHO Egypt Country Office to provide dialysis treatment for Sudanese refugees in Egypt due to the ongoing conflict in Sudan.

GKB has announced actress Sanya Malhotra as its brand ambassador as the premium eyewear brand unveiled its new identity and marked the opening of its 100th store in India. Sanya Malhotra becomes brand ambassador for GKB as eyewear brand opens 100th store
As part of the transformation, GKB Opticals will now operate under the name GKB. With its new identity, the appointment of Sanya Malhotra and the opening of its 100th store, GKB is looking to strengthen its position in the premium eyewear market by combining its established legacy with fashion, design and technological innovation.

Omani Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash plane into Israeli airport, UAE says
The planned suicide attack was inspired by the events of September 11 in the US, public prosecutors believe
An Omani Flydubai co-pilot had intended to seize a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight and crash it into a terminal at Israel’s Ben Gurion airport on September 30 in a suicide attack before he was thwarted by his fellow pilot, the UAE attorney general said on Friday, according to the state news agency.

Flydubai was not immediately available for comment.
The plan was inspired by the September 11, 2001, attacks on the US, UAE public prosecutors think as a result of their criminal investigation launched on October 1.

Our skin, hair and nails require adequate protein, energy, vitamins and minerals for growth, repair and normal functioning. When deficiencies are significant or prolonged, some may become visible. But many of these signs also overlap with hormonal disorders, chronic illnesses, dermatological conditions, stress, poor sleep and other factors. So when and how do you know if there is a nutritional deficit?
What the signs can indicate
Iron deficiency, particularly when it progresses to anaemia, can cause pallor of the skin and mucous membranes, and may be associated with diffuse hair shedding. Spoon-shaped nails can also occur with iron deficiency. Vitamin B12 deficiency may cause hyperpigmentation, particularly over the knuckles, as well as changes in the tongue and oral mucosa.
Zinc deficiency can affect skin integrity and hair growth, while inadequate protein intake can affect hair structure and growth and, in severe cases, cause marked changes in the skin and hair. Vitamin C deficiency can result in bleeding gums and poor wound healing. Dry or scaly skin may be associated with inadequate vitamin A, essential fatty acids or zinc.
Cracks at the corners of the mouth can occur with iron, vitamin B12, zinc or riboflavin deficiency. A smooth, red and sore tongue, or glossitis, can be associated with deficiencies of vitamin B12, iron, folate or niacin.
Ramya Subburaj, senior clinical dietitian and head of the department of dietetics, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Vanagaram, Chennai, said these signs should be viewed as clues rather than proof of a deficiency. “There is considerable overlap between nutritional and non-nutritional causes,” she said, noting that a person with hair loss should not assume that poor nutrition is necessarily responsible.
What ‘ferritin face’ really means
Terms such as ‘iron-deficiency face’ and ‘ferritin face’ circulating on social media are not recognised medical diagnoses. Iron deficiency can cause anaemia and pallor, but there is no specific facial appearance through which low ferritin can be diagnosed.
Ferritin is a protein that stores iron and its level is used to assess the body’s iron stores. Low ferritin can occur before iron-deficiency anaemia develops. However, it does not produce a distinct facial appearance.
Pushpa Gnanaraj, senior consultant, dermatology, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, said pallor associated with anaemia may be visible in the skin, lips, gums or inner eyelids because of reduced haemoglobin. But dullness, dark circles or changes in facial appearance are not specific to low iron stores.
Vinitha Krishnan, chief clinical dietitian, nutrition and dietetics, SIMS Hospital, Chennai, said any changes associated with depleted iron stores are generally subtle and non-specific. Similar features can occur with inadequate sleep, stress, dehydration, allergies, ageing, thyroid disorders or other nutritional deficiencies.
A proper history and clinical examination are therefore important. Depending on the symptoms, investigations may include a complete blood count, ferritin and iron studies, vitamin B12 and vitamin D. Thyroid testing, zinc assessment or other investigations may be considered when clinically indicated. Dermatological conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, fungal infections, autoimmune disorders and pigmentary diseases may also need to be ruled out.
Correcting deficiencies
When a confirmed nutritional deficiency is responsible for a symptom, correcting it can lead to improvement. The timeline, however, depends on the nutrient involved and the severity and duration of the deficiency.
Pallor and some symptoms associated with iron deficiency may begin to improve within weeks of appropriate treatment, while mouth ulcers and glossitis can also improve after the underlying deficiency is corrected. Hair shedding and thinning generally take longer to recover because hair grows slowly; improvement may take several months. Nail changes can similarly take months to grow out.
Reshma Aleem, senior clinical dietician, Rela Hospital, Chennai, said the extent and speed of recovery depend on whether the deficiency is mild, moderate or severe and on how effectively it is corrected.
Fixing the basics
A varied diet remains the foundation. Adequate protein, pulses, whole grains, vegetables, fruits, nuts and seeds, along with eggs, dairy, fish, lean meat or fortified foods according to dietary preference, can provide a range of nutrients.
Experts caution against taking supplements based only on a social-media checklist. Excessive intake of some vitamins and minerals can itself cause adverse effects and may interfere with the absorption or metabolism of other nutrients. More importantly, treating an assumed deficiency can delay the diagnosis of the actual cause.
The appropriate approach is to investigate persistent changes, confirm a deficiency where indicated and then correct it with dietary measures or supplementation under clinical guidance.

Many Nepalis swept away in the floods aren't officially dead, leaving families in limbo
- Published
At the Pashupatinath temple, on the banks of the Bagmati River in Kathmandu, Madan Lal Lawat joined other families in honouring loved ones who were lost when a deadly flood tore through the China-Nepal border last month.
In Hindu tradition, when a body cannot be recovered, a symbolic effigy is made from sacred "kusha" grass to represent the dead, allowing relatives to perform last rites.
With more than 5,000 people still missing and the government ending rescue operations, this is the only way people like Lawat can honour the dead.
Five of his relatives - including his brother - were caught in the water's onslaught and are still missing. Lawat survived because he was driving his bus outside his village, Betrawati.
The last Lawat heard from survivors is that his brother Mangal died while going door-to-door, trying to warn others to leave.
"I don't know how to start over. Police say they're still searching for the bodies, but I'm not sure they'll ever be found," Lawat says.
He has little doubt they are dead.
But legally, their fate is far more complicated. In Nepal, a missing person is only presumed dead after 12 years.
Section 40 of Nepal's Civil Code does allow for some exceptions, but it does not have a provision for disasters like the flood witnessed last month.
Families like Lawat's have told the BBC they are struggling to obtain death certificates, affecting everything from accessing flood compensation to the transfer of properties and even inheritance.
Relatives can receive up to 25,000 rupees (£122; $162) for funeral costs, in addition to about 200,000 rupees (£981; $1,302) in bereavement compensation for the first relative who died, and 100,000 rupees (£491; $651) for each additional death.
But this is only possible once they submit a death certificate. So as families try to rebuild their lives, many are now caught in an administrative nightmare.
"In view of the current disaster, the law is outdated," says constitutional law expert, Bipin Adhikari.
He explains the law was meant to account for people who travelled abroad and weren't heard from for years. "But technology has advanced now, it isn't as difficult to send or receive information," he argues.
For Lawat, the legal minefield has made an already devastating loss even harder to navigate.
When he tried to obtain a death certificate last week, officials at the local municipality office turned him away. "They said they're still discussing the death certificate issue. We aren't sure what to do now. There's so much uncertainty," he tells us.
Even when bodies are recovered, identifying their identities is a slow and challenging task. More than 1,400 bodies have been recovered so far, and Nepal has little experience in processing DNA at such scale. In some cases, authorities have taken DNA samples, then buried the bodies with markers in the ground, should families claim them.
Given the scale of damage and loss, families say compensation is desperately needed.
Nepal's latest assessment counts 7,570 private buildings damaged or destroyed, home to nearly 33,000 people based on census data.
The BBC visited Lawat's village Betrawati just days after the disaster, once the roads to the district of Rasuwa had been cleared. For days, this area had been cut off from the capital Kathmandu, and struggling with a shortage of basic supplies including petrol.
The damage in the village was staggering. The ground was nothing but hardened mud and silt. Footage of the flood showed it had swallowed most of the village in just minutes. There was no sign of its bustling market, the local Uttargaya School was in ruins, the houses swept away, and school buses were turned over.
Betrawati straddles flood-devastated Rasuwa and Nuwakot, and is part of the Bidur municipality, where the government estimates more than 3,000 buildings have been damaged or destroyed. It's the largest amount of any municipality.
Local governments are now urging the prime minister's office to figure out a way to resolve the death confirmation issue.
"Everything is on hold," Bidur's Mayor, Rajan Shrestha, told the BBC.
He said it could take up to 12 years for relatives to access the funds they are entitled to.
For one of South Asia's smallest economies, finding money for compensation is a challenge, and the sums on offer are small when compared with the scale of the losses.
The government puts damage to personal belongings alone at £123 million ($165 million) across more than 8,300 households.
This implies losses of about £14,800 ($20,000) on average per household, though this figure is only based on census data and modelling, and doesn't represent the exact cost per family.
The financial toll makes the death certificates vital for families trying to recover from the disaster.
Shrestha is calling on the federal government to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Until then, he says his hands are tied.
"We understand the emotional pain for families who have already performed funeral rituals, but officials must work within legal boundaries to avoid future liabilities."
The government has told the BBC it is trying to find a solution.
In a statement, the prime minister's office said it was "aware of the difficulties" the law may cause families in "exceptional circumstances, including disasters". The home ministry said the government was taking the issue seriously and was ready to amend the law, if required.
The legal hurdles families are facing comes as Nepal faces a steep reconstruction bill, which the government says could cost up to £3.6bn ($4.8bn).
At the UN General Assembly in New York, Prime Minister Balen Shah explained rebuilding the country would require more than 10% of its gross domestic product, an enormous burden on the country's economy.
Dozens of public buildings including schools, health clinics and hospitals have been wrecked by the floods. That's in addition to roads, bridges, wastewater treatment plants and hydropower projects.
Shah is now pushing for grant-based international support rather than new loans. Nepal is one of the lowest emitters of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet one one of the most vulnerable countries to global warming.
"When a climate-driven disaster destroys infrastructure of a poor country, the answer cannot simply be another mega-loan or a patchwork of small grants," he told a room full of world leaders.
This is not the first time Nepal has had to recover after a devastating natural disaster.
For Tisum Ghale, the past month has been painfully familiar.
He and his family lost their home in an earthquake in 2015, and became displaced for months. They eventually settled in Betrawati.
But the place that was once a refuge is where 19 of his relatives were killed in last month's flood, including five of his sisters. He survived because he was doing construction work outside of the village.
Once again, he is without a home.
"I have lost everything," he said.
So far he has received no compensation. He desperately needs the money after his home was washed away and he looks after eight children left behind by his sisters. He is one of the thousands displaced, living across 37 holding centres in northern Nepal.
Like Lawati and thousands of other families, Ghale plans on holding a funeral without his loved ones' bodies.
He hopes the law will eventually recognise what he already knows: his loved ones will not be coming home.

Generic drugmaker Granules India has filed a Paragraph IV certification with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (U.S. FDA) in connection with its abbreviated new drug application (ANDA) for Ruxolitinib Extended-Release Tablets.
Based on the timing and status of its ANDA and Paragraph IV certification, and subject to the U.S. FDA’s review and determination, Granules said it believes it is eligible for first-to-file status for Ruxolitinib Extended-Release Tablets.
If confirmed by the FDA and subject to all applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, first-to-file status could make Granules eligible for 180 days of generic drug exclusivity under U.S. law, the company said on Wednesday (September 7, 2026).
The Paragraph IV certification sought is with respect to applicable patents listed in the U.S. FDA’s Orange Book. Granules said it has also issued the requisite notice to the relevant parties in accordance with U.S. regulatory requirements.
“First-to-file opportunities are an important part of our strategy to build a more differentiated and higher-value product portfolio in the U.S. This filing reflects our focus on identifying technically and commercially attractive opportunities where our development and manufacturing capabilities can create sustainable value,” Granules CMD Krishna Prasad Chigurupati said.
Ruxolitinib, a JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor, was approved by the U.S. FDA in 2011 and is used to treat certain cancers and related conditions. In the U.S., the drug is developed and marketed by Incyte Corporation under the brand name Jakafi. Jakafi and Jakafi XR are trademarks of Incyte.
In May, Nasdaq-listed Incyte announced that the U.S. FDA had approved Jakafi XR, the extended-release formulation of ruxolitinib.
The drug is marketed by Incyte in the U.S. and by Novartis outside the country under the brand name Jakavi.

On 02 October 2026, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has called for a mass protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on 10 October 2026, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the voter rolls. The CJP is also demanding an immediate halt to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and the restoration of all names removed since 25 June 2025. Left-wing student organisations have also issued a joint statement announcing that they will join the demonstration in large numbers.
In this context, several videos (here, here, here, here & here) are circulating on social media claiming that members of Hindu organisations, such as the Bajrang Dal, have begun moving towards Jantar Mantar to oppose the protest. Let’s verify the authenticity of these claims.
Claim: Viral videos show Hindu groups, including Bajrang Dal, mobilising activists to oppose the CJP protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on 10 October 2026.
Fact: All these videos predate the protest announcement and depict unrelated events, including a Ram Navami bike rally in West Bengal, BJP victory celebrations, and Chhatrapati Shivaji’s coronation anniversary celebrations. Bajrang Dal has also denied plans to mobilise volunteers at Jantar Mantar. Hence, the claims made in these posts are False.
Video 1:
A reverse image search of keyframes extracted from the viral video revealed that the same video (archived) has been available since at least November 2022. Although the exact context of the original video remains unclear, we found that the clip has been repeatedly repurposed for various issues over the years. This confirms that the viral video has no connection to the Jantar Mantar protest on 10 October 2026.
Video 2:
Our investigation revealed that this video, depicting a bike rally, has been available (archived) since at least 28 March 2026. It shows a bike rally from Chandrakona Road to Garhbeta in West Bengal to mark the occasion of Ram Navami. This confirms that the footage even predates the formation of the CJP movement.
Video 3:
We analysed another video of the bike rally and found that it has been available (archived) since 04 May 2026. It depicts celebrations following the BJP’s historic victory in West Bengal, featuring a procession of people waving saffron flags and raising religious slogans.
Video 4:
This video, showing people rallying on the road with saffron flags, has been available (archived) online since at least 09 September 2026. Although the exact context of the clip remains unknown, the footage was uploaded more than three weeks before the announcement of the Jantar Mantar protest.
Video 5:
This video, which features large crowds, has been available (archived) online since at least June 2026. It depicts the crowd at the coronation anniversary celebrations of Chhatrapati Shivaji at Raigad Fort, held on 6 June 2026.
Similarly, some unverified clips are being shared, claiming to show the arrival of Bajrang Dal activists at Jantar Mantar to oppose the protest. However, the Bajrang Dal has rejected these claims. In a clarification (archived) on X, the organisation stated it has no plans to mobilise volunteers or assemble at Jantar Mantar on October 10, adding that some individuals are spreading misleading propaganda.
To sum it up, old, unrelated videos are being circulated with the false claim that they show Hindu activists mobilising at Jantar Mantar to oppose the CJP protest

They have fun names like Feel Free, Smurphs, and Hazy Tabz. They come in colorful packages and in gummy form. They’re widely available at gas stations, corner stores, and smoke shops across the country.
The rise of gas station opioids
What are kratom and 7-OH, the opioid-like drugs that you can buy at the gas station?
They’re also highly addictive, largely unregulated, and in the news after they were found near the bodies of two dead University of Mississippi students.
The drugs are called Kratom and 7-OH. The first, kratom, is derived from the leaves of a coffee-like plant in Southeast Asia. When taken in small doses, kratom causes a low-key buzz. In higher doses, the high is described as euphoric. It operates like an opioid — a chemical in kratom called mitragynine binds to opioid receptors in the brain, which leads to that euphoric high. It also can lead to addiction and overdose.
Social media is full of videos of people trying to kick the drug, with harrowing stories of dependence and withdrawal.
7-OH is a highly concentrated compound derived from kratom, which dials up both the high and the danger. The drug has caught the attention of US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who warned in a press conference last year that 7-OH was “marketed for children.”
“They’re gummy bears, they’re bright colors, they’re candy-flavored,” Kennedy said. “This is really a sinister, sinister industry.” In August, federal agencies announced they were taking steps to effectively ban 7-OH nationwide.
To break down the increasing prevalence of both kratom and 7-OH, what the drugs do, and what to do about them, Today, Explained spoke with Mattha Busby, a freelance journalist who covers drugs and drug policy and who wrote about kratom earlier this year.
As Busby explains, kratom and 7-OH are “definitely in the zeitgeist. It’s in the news and for good reason. To have these 7-OH gummies just in gas stations is a really potentially problematic thing. Without the drug education alongside it, this drug has just popped up out of nowhere.”
Busby also talked with Today, Explained co-host Sean Rameswaram about the business interests behind the drugs, why they’re a complicated topic for the Make America Healthy Again movement, and how industry lobbyists have teamed up with several Trump administration officials to try to sway the results of regulatory decisions.
Below is an excerpt of their conversation, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full podcast, so listen to Today, Explained wherever you get podcasts, including Apple Podcasts, Pandora, and Spotify.
Is there an important distinction between kratom and 7-OH? Is 7-OH found in kratom?
7-OH is found in relatively small quantities within kratom, but this businessman, Vince Saunders, who is the self-styled American shaman out of Kansas City, basically figured out how to extract the 7-OH and blow it up into entire pills.
I’ve never tried 7-OH and I’m not interested, just for the record, since I’ve been talking about how I don’t mind kratom, but these 7-OH tablets are uber, uber strong. I think the large number of people that are taking it are using it instead of opioids. And maybe it’s better, maybe it’s not.
Is 7-OH something you can also easily find at your neighborhood gas station?
Yeah. It’s much the same as the kratom formulations, so you’re talking gummies, little shots, capsules, and the brand names for the 7-OH companies are perhaps even more kind of out there — 7-OHeaven is one.
It’s certainly not heaven when you’re going into withdrawals.
And do we know that people are? Are people becoming addicted to 7-OH?
People are becoming addicted to kratom and 7-OH. I think the whole thing, the concern originally sprung up with the Feel Free tonics that are like a mix of kava and kratom. And people just got habituated into drinking several of them per day and realized that it’s very unpleasant if they don’t continue to do that on a daily basis.
We have a federal government that loves to police drugs of all sorts. What are they doing about 7-OH?
It’s this MAHA dilemma, right? Because their ethos is very “natural medicines and freedom.” The idea that this Feel Free tonic, whose owner JW Ross recently gave, or a company related to him recently gave, like $500,000 to the MAHA PAC, and he’s been photographed next to RFK Jr. — he’s perhaps predictably come out on the side of the kratom industry, which is lobbying for a ban of 7-OH.
RFK Jr. called it sinister and said that it targets children, which it appears to do in some cases with the gummies. There’s kratom gummies too and clearly gummies are an easier way, especially for older people, to ingest the medicine or substance, so we shouldn’t just blame the gummies here.
But clearly, when you’ve just got packets of these gummies that are called like 7-OHeaven just on the shelf or indeed behind the counter at the gas station, there’s going to be concern about that.
There are other MAGA figures like Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who’s got a million-dollar investment in the parent company of Feel Free. There’s definitely this nexus of figures in the government that have got some interest, potentially, or relationships with the kratom industry. And indeed the department when I was writing my Wired story reminded us and readers that everything he’s done is ethical and I’m sure it has been.
We usually think of liberal drug policies as a lefty thing. Markwayne Mullin’s about as right as they come. Are kratom and 7-OH making friends across the political spectrum because there’s a big business opportunity here?
You look at Trump’s executive order on psychedelics and then rescheduling cannabis, and it seems that the right has really seized the mantle and is looking at it from a more libertarian perspective of, “Hey, what happens in a man’s head is his own business.”
They’re also being probably more business friendly than people on the left would be, so it’s a really interesting moment, especially with RFK Jr. as health secretary.
Trump has spoken at length about the opioid crisis in the United States and how it’s tearing our communities apart and whatnot. Here we have readily accessible opioids at our gas stations.
Yes, they’re not killing nearly as many people as prescription drugs are. However, they’re a lot easier to get than prescription drugs. Help me understand this administration’s position in relation to what could be a real terror for some people.
They are in the process of banning 7-OH. Last month, the Department of Justice set out an emergency scheduling, so that’s open for comments at the moment. When they ban something, it doesn’t just happen overnight.
I think by the beginning of next year, it’s quite possible that these 7-OH products won’t be in gas stations and indeed some states have already taken action.
And just to get ahead of any confusion here, 7-OH may be banned from gas stations and probably other convenience stores, but not kratom?
Exactly.
Why one and not the other? Obviously 7-OH is stronger, but you could take a lot of kratom and it might feel like taking a little 7-OH, no?
Absolutely. You just need to take a lot and it’s in powder form. So you need to consume a prodigious quantity of it or drink a bunch of these seltzers.
I think that they’re not going to ban kratom because there’s an obvious recognition of the good it does for people that are recovering from opiate addictions and that they do have a kind of natural off-ramp, [which] is very unlikely to kill you even though you might take a huge amount. Whereas, if you’re taking like 26 different medications, including a bunch of opioids for your chronic pain, you might die.
Who do you think wins the argument at the end of the day? We have some strong lobbying forces involved here. You’ve got a lot of people who have come to enjoy or depend on these substances that are, as we’ve established many times now, readily available all over the country.
Do you think we see fewer or more kratom products in our gas stations and convenience stores in the years to come?
The kratom advocates are a lot more eloquent and suited and booted than the 7-OH folks. What I see is that 7-OH will be forced underground and that kratom will continue its long and illustrious ascent in American culture.
We do really have a gas station culture in this country, and I wonder if these substances being so available in them is a particularly American thing. You live in the UK. Are gas station drugs a US thing?
It’s an American thing for sure. But you guys take a lot of drugs!

Craig Zobel, a director known for his work on such prestige series as Mare of Easttown and The Penguin, is set to direct a feature adaptation of Something Is Killing the Children, the popular comic book series from James Tynion IV and Werther Dell’Edera, with Jason Blum and his Blumhouse among the producers.
Stephen Christy and Tynion IV will produce the film for BOOM! Studios/Penguin Random House, alongside Blum for Blumhouse. Shaun Sutton and Ryan Turek will exec produce alongside Adam Yoelin and Mette Norkjaer, with Dell’Edera acting as co-producer.
The news came out of New York Comic-Con, where Blumhouse laid out its 2027 slate.
Watch on Deadline
First published by BOOM! Studios, an imprint of Penguin Random House, in 2019, Something is Killing the Children centers on Erica Slaughter, a monster hunter who arrives in the small town of Archer’s Peak after children begin disappearing to take down the creature preying on them. It’s the most successful original horror comic book since The Walking Dead, with more than 5 million copies sold worldwide, having been translated into more than 20 languages in 14 countries.
While developing the live-action feature, Blumhouse is simultaneously developing an adult animated series version of Something Is Killing the Children to be shepherded by Tynion IV.
A DGA Award nominee and three-time Emmy nominee, Zobel broke out with indies like Compliance and Z for Zachariah before going on to work on shows such as The Leftovers, American Gods, Westworld, Mare of Easttown and The Penguin. He also helmed the satirical horror film The Hunt and just wrapped production on Turpentine, a new thriller starring Melissa McCarthy and Connie Storrie.
